exercises.title: Product champion 1 — who makes a good champion?
exercises.problemHtml:
A product champion is the primary interface between one user class and the BA — ideally an actual user, not a surrogate (sponsor, marketing, a manager, or a developer imagining being a user). Good champions have a clear vision of the system, are enthusiastic, respected by their peers, and have time and authority to decide at the user-requirements level.

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.

exercises.title: Product champion 2 — trap or healthy practice?
exercises.problemHtml:
Traps: managers overriding a duly authorised champion; a champion pushing only personal requirements; a champion without vision who defers everything to the BA; a senior user nominating a junior and then back-seat driving; anyone claiming to speak for a user class without really representing it. Classify each situation.

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.

exercises.title: Product champion 3 — external and multiple champions
exercises.problemHtml:
For commercial software, outside champions are hard to find: use close corporate customers, beta sites or internal SMEs. With a diverse customer base, first find the core requirements common to all, then add those specific to segments or user classes. One person rarely covers all users: set up a team of champions, possibly with backup teams (Don the chemist built a backup team of five chemists).

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.

exercises.title: Product champion 4 — communication pathways
exercises.problemHtml:
The most direct path from user to developer is a developer talking to users — workable only on very small projects. Every intervening layer adds miscommunication and delay, but a skilled BA adds value by collecting, evaluating, refining and organising input. Goal: as few, and as high-value, layers as possible. User representatives must be involved throughout the life cycle, not only at the start.

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.
